item.text: {"text":"SASRec scores each causal prefix against item embeddings ([original implementation](https://github.com/kang205/SASRec/blob/master/model.py)). A proposed residual can use learned decay ρ=sigmoid(a), valid-item mask mₜ, and xₜ=√d·E[sₜ], matching SASRec’s input embedding scale. Initialize numerator u₀=0 and weight z₀=0; update uₜ=ρuₜ₋₁+mₜxₜ and zₜ=ρzₜ₋₁+mₜ, then rₜ=uₜ/clamp(zₜ,ε). Left-padding contributes nothing; explicitly zero padded outputs. Fuse fₜ=mₜ·[hₜ+γ·LN(rₜ)], with learned γ and parameter-free normalization using `F.layer_norm(r, (d,), weight=None, bias=None)` ([PyTorch documentation](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/main/generated/torch.nn.LayerNorm.html)). This is an implementation proposal, not an established SASRec result. The recurrence adds O(BLd) work and O(Bd) running state; retaining every prefix and autograd intermediates requires O(BLd) memory. SASRec attention cost remains unchanged, and a Python loop introduces L sequential launches.\n\nMake `log2feats(sequence)` return these fused features everywhere. Training computes positive/negative logits as elementwise dot products with the corresponding unscaled target embeddings; preserve that same target scaling in diagnostics and inference. Define `predict_score(features, items)` explicitly for aligned items and shared/per-user candidate sets, avoiding ambiguous broadcasting. Final inference scores the last valid fused feature; index −1 works for nonempty, left-padded sequences. Update the predictor writer to reconstruct this architecture and load decay/gain parameters. Numerical checks should compare recurrence outputs and gradients with explicit normalized geometric sums, verify padding invariance and causal independence, compare training/diagnostic/inference logits in evaluation mode, and confirm checkpoint round-trip parity. These checks establish implementation consistency, not validation improvement."}
